hook: This is a long, character-driven file about six cybernetically altered outlaws who call themselves the Black Rabbit Company. Most of it is a set of intake interviews, each with a very different voice, ranging from cheerful storytelling to flat refusal to open hostility. Content note: it contains crude language, references to violent operations and a passage about self-harm, all presented in report form.
whyItMatters: It is a humanoid-group file whose interest lies less in an anomalous effect than in people and their politics. A timeline of internal motions shows Foundation departments arguing over what should happen to the subjects, which puts the organization's own ethics on the table. The cat-themed modifications and the superhero tag set up a pulpy, comic-book flavour that the file then complicates with frank talk about illness, captivity and mortality.
thingsToNotice: Each interview works as a character sketch, and the aliases borrowed from fiction, explained in a footnote, are part of how the members present themselves. Notice how often the subjects talk about one another rather than themselves, which makes the bond within the group the real subject. A line about a star and the morning appears in more than one interview, tying the first voice to the last. The final interview gives the thing living inside one member a voice of sorts, set against his own reasons for carrying on.
